horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Test a small agriculture business, validate demand, build supplier and customer relationships, and learn basic business operations.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Focus on one business model: organic inputs, farm services, produce aggregation, nursery operations, value addition, or farm advisory.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Build repeatable operations, reliable quality controls, distribution, a team, and a financially viable customer base.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Adapt to climate risks, changing consumer demand, traceability requirements, digital sales, and new agricultural technologies.

blocks.text: Build an agriculture-based business that solves a real farming or food-market problem, tests demand with customers, and grows sustainably through sound production, pricing, and operations.

blocks.label: Current degree
blocks.text: B.Sc – Natural Farming / Organic Agriculture

blocks.label: Desired career
blocks.text: Agri Entrepreneur

blocks.label: Career cluster
blocks.text: Agribusiness, sustainable agriculture, food systems, and rural enterprise

blocks.label: Timeline assumption
blocks.text: This roadmap assumes a three-year B.Sc. beginning in 2026 and completion around 2029. A four-year honours or research pathway can provide an additional year to test a business idea, conduct market research, or complete an incubation programme. The exact course-to-career taxonomy mapping could not be verified, so this is a cluster-level roadmap.
These are planning horizons, not verified forecasts of business success or market demand.
Semester-by-semester plan

rows.text: Interview 15 farmers or potential customers about one problem, such as compost availability, produce wastage, or farm labour.
Interview notes and a ranked list of customer problems.
Compare three possible business models and estimate basic costs and selling prices.
One-page business model and a break-even estimate.
Test a small product or service, such as a nursery batch, compost trial, farm-record service, or direct-produce sale.
A pilot record showing costs, customers, feedback, and unsold stock.
Build a supplier, production, quality, packaging, and delivery plan.
Supplier list, quality checklist, and delivery workflow.
Complete an internship or incubation programme and speak with prospective buyers.
Mentor feedback and evidence of repeat customer interest.
Run a measured pilot and prepare a launch decision.
Cash-flow forecast, customer feedback, unit economics, and a go/no-go decision.

blocks.label: Four-year honours variant
blocks.text: Use the extra year to validate demand across seasons, improve production or sourcing systems, conduct a supervised business study, and explore incubation or funding. Do not borrow heavily before proving demand and understanding the risks.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Grow from founder-operated sales to dependable systems, documented quality, reliable suppliers, and repeat customers. Adopt digital inventory, customer management, traceability, and climate-risk planning where they solve real problems. Expand only when the economics and operational capacity support it.

blocks.label: Eligibility note
blocks.text: You do not need to register a company just to test a business idea. Start with lawful, low-cost customer validation. Before selling food, seeds, fertilisers, pesticides, or other regulated products, check the applicable licences, product standards, and local rules.
For an Agri Entrepreneur, practical market validation and financial discipline usually matter more than collecting certificates. Choose training that addresses your intended business model.

2040–2046: Build a business that can withstand changes in weather, input costs, buyer expectations, and regulation. Track customer retention, profit per product or service, working capital, wastage, supplier reliability, and environmental outcomes. Use technology where it reduces costs or improves service, not just to appear innovative.
